items.title: No repeat of Dataran Merdeka mess, says Hannah Yeoh
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Members of the public attending the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31 have been urged to act responsibly by disposing of their rubbish at designated areas to ensure the venue remains clean. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she did not want a repeat of the recent incident at Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur, where large amounts of rubbish were left behind following a public gathering. "Imagine coming to celebrate National Day, only to leave behind an area covered with rubbish.

items.title: Bukit Aman awaits Indonesian details after Malaysian pilot arrested with drugs at Jakarta airport
items.summary: Narcotic Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police are awaiting further details from their counterparts before determining the next course of action, the New Straits Times (NST) reported. Hussein told NST that investigators also wanted to determine how many times the suspect might have carried out similar operations and whether he was part of a wider network. Investigators are also examining how the suspect allegedly managed to pass through airport security in Malaysia before departing for Indonesia.

items.title: Negri polls: Voter turnout reaches 51.58pct as at 2pm
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Voter turnout for the Negri Sembilan election reached 51.58 per cent as at 2 pm. The Election Commission, in its hourly update, said 443,461 of the 859,760 eligible ordinary voters had cast their ballots. Early voting on July 28 recorded a turnout of 91.06 per cent, with 14,995 voters casting their ballots.

items.title: Homecoming rush: Voters return, traffic builds across Negri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Traffic flow on several major routes around Seremban, as well as connecting roads to outlying districts such as Bukit Putus, Kuala Pilah and Kuala Klawang in Jelebu, has been reported to be steadily building since early this morning. Real-time traffic checks on Google Maps, Waze and Apple Maps revealed slow-moving traffic at several hotspots, particularly along the Seremban-Kuala Pilah road through Bukit Putus, the Seremban-Tampin route, and roads leading to Kuala Klawang in Jelebu. Meanwhile, Negri Sembilan Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Supt Roslan Mohamed@Ab Aziz, when contacted, said conditions remained under control as of 2pm despite the noticeable increase in vehicles.

items.title: ‘Shared responsibility’: Hannah Yeoh urges public to help maintain cleanliness during Putrajaya National Day celebration
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 1 — Members of the public attending the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31 have been urged to act responsibly by disposing of their rubbish at designated areas to ensure the venue remains clean. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she does not want a repeat of the recent incident at Dataran Merdeka, Kuala Lumpur, where large amounts of rubbish were left behind following a public gathering. “Imagine coming to celebrate National Day, only to leave behind an area covered with rubbish.

items.title: Tun Jugah-inspired hairstyle draws crowds at KJH Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING: Sarawak Tourism Board (STB) marketing administrative officer Ozie Tunggeng has been turning heads at the Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) Sarawak Segulai Sejalai with a distinctive hairstyle inspired by the legendary Iban leader, Tun Jugah anak Barieng. Throughout the carnival, Ozie has been promoting the state's tourism products and hosting interactive stage activities, including tourism quizzes. STB assistant marketing officer Nabil Aiman Sait said the board remains committed to promoting Sarawak's tourism offerings to both domestic and international visitors.

items.title: Mental health stigma leaves many suffering in silence, says Queen
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has expressed concern that the stigma surrounding mental health continues to prevent many people from seeking professional help, leaving them to suffer in silence. Citing New Straits Times reports on the growing mental health crisis, Her Majesty said adults were increasingly burdened by financial hardship, debt and strained family relationships, often leading to severe psychological distress. Raja Zarith Sofiah, who received an Honorary Doctorate in Psychology from the university, said addressing the nation's mental health challenges had never been more important.

items.title: Police tighten security at Negeri Sembilan palace, state offices ahead of poll results
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Police will tighten security at key locations, including the Istana of the Yang di Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan and state government offices, to prevent any untoward incidents when the Negeri Sembilan state election results are announced later tonight. Inspector General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said there was a possibility that certain quarters might attempt to stir tensions if dissatisfied with the outcome, Sinar Harian reported. Mohd Khalid was speaking to reporters after visiting the polling centre at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan King George V here today.

items.title: Chief Justice heads Pahang state honours list
items.summary: Also present were the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang, Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah. Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail and state government leaders were also in attendance. Wan Ahmad Farid was conferred the Sri Setia Al-Sultan Abdullah Ahmad Shah Pahang (SAAS) award, which carries the title of Datuk Seri Setia.

items.title: Nerves, pride as 1st time voters cast their ballots
items.summary: SEREMBAN: For many first-time voters in the 16th Negri Sembilan election today, casting their ballot was a memorable milestone marked by excitement, nerves and pride. Fashion designer Hani Eriqa Mazlan, 21, said voting for the first time gave her a deeper appreciation of the democratic process. "I was nervous and my hands were shaking because it was my first time voting.

items.title: CAP calls for tougher screening for pilots after Jakarta drug case
items.summary: CAP president Mohideen Abdul Kader said the association was "shocked and disappointed" by the incident, calling it a major blow to Malaysia's aviation industry and public confidence in air travel. He said passenger safety must remain the highest priority, as travellers entrust their lives to pilots every time they board an aircraft. "Passengers expect pilots to be responsible for their lives on a flight.

items.title: Negri polls: Voter turnout reaches 44.67pct as at 1pm
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Voter turnout for the Negri Sembilan election reached 44.67 per cent as at 1 pm. The Election Commission, in its hourly update, said 384,096 of the 859,760 eligible ordinary voters had cast their ballots. Early voting on July 28 recorded a turnout of 91.06 per cent, with 14,995 voters casting their ballots.

items.title: Bukit Aman to work with Indonesian police in probe involving Malaysian pilot
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman will work closely with their Indonesian counterparts in the investigation involving a Malaysian pilot arrested in Indonesia for allegedly attempting to smuggle drugs into the country. Bukit Aman Narcotic Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan told the New Straits Times that police are awaiting more information from Indonesian authorities before determining the next course of action. Hussein said police are also studying the need to send a team of investigators to Indonesia to interview the suspect to establish the full circumstances surrounding the case.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan confirms two Undang appointments, declares three other claimants invalid
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has formally recognised two newly installed Undang and declared three individuals who claimed the titles of Undang Sungei Ujong, Rembau and Jelebu as never having held those positions lawfully. Muhammad Faris Johari was formerly recognised as the Undang Luak Sungei Ujong, while Raja Hassan Ab Hamid’s appointment as Undang Luak Rembau was also affirmed under adat. The DKU also noted that the position of the position of Undang for Sungei Ujong is now vacant after the previous holder, Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid, was removed according to adat effective 30 July 2026.

items.title: Police tighten security, urge supporters to accept poll results
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Police have urged political party supporters to remain calm and accept the outcome of the Negri Sembilan election, with security measures in place to handle any eventuality. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said police were prepared to manage any situation, including a possible change in the state administration following the election results. "Police are responsible for maintaining security not only before and during the election, but also after polling.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan election sees 37pc voter turnout by noon
items.summary: The Election Commission (EC), in a Facebook post, said the Juasseh constituency recorded the highest voter turnout so far at 43.5 per cent, followed by Chennah (43.4 per cent) and Senaling (42.8 per cent). The Lukut constituency recorded the lowest turnout at about 32.1 per cent. For comparison, voter turnout at the same time during the 15th Negeri Sembilan state election stood at 35.44 per cent, or 297,024 of the 838,200 registered voters.

items.title: Local councils must review dog-catching procedures
items.summary: The circumstances surrounding his death have caused widespread public outrage. One principle must remain clear: Local authorities must never resort to excessive force, brutality or cruelty in carrying out their duties. Whether a dog is a pet or a stray, licensed or unlicensed, every animal must be treated humanely.

items.title: 92 reports, 24 probe papers opened during Negri poll campaign
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Police received 92 reports and opened 24 investigation papers during the campaign period for the Negri Sembilan election, which ended at midnight, says Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail. He said most cases involved offences under the Election Offences Act, including acts of mischief such as damage to political parties' banners and flags. "From nomination day on July 18 until today, we received 92 police reports and opened 24 investigation papers.

items.title: Negri Sembilan polls: Polling day adds unique twist to Kuala Pilah couple's wedding
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: A Negri Sembilan couple's wedding became even more memorable after their big day coincided with the state's polling day, prompting the groom to head to the ballot box before the marriage ceremony. Dentist Zulhid Rosmawi, 32, said he and his family had fixed the wedding date about six months ago, long before the Election Commission announced Aug 1 as polling day. Despite the coincidence, Zulhid said preparations for the ceremony went ahead as planned.

items.title: TH: 2017 accounts could have shown RM1.4bil loss under accounting rules
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) said its 2017 financial statement would have recorded a loss if it had fully adopted the Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS). TH said the RCI's findings on the use of the Realisable Asset Value (RAV) method reinforced the need for financial statements to be prepared transparently, consistently and in accordance with established accounting standards. The practice affected TH's financial reserves and created expectations among depositors for consistently high dividend payouts, the report said.

items.title: Police to record Sanusi's statement in Kedah
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Police will record the statement of Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor over remarks he allegedly made touching on racial issues during a political rally in Jempol recently. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the case remained under investigation. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad had said they received a report over a speech delivered by the Jeneri assemblyman.

items.title: Sisters turn polling day into patriotic parade of Jalur Gemilang [WATCH]
items.summary: REMBAU: Two siblings turned heads at the polling centre in Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Chung Hua, Rantau today after arriving dressed in Jalur Gemilang-themed outfits, adding a patriotic touch to the voting atmosphere. Eldest sister Zamzarina Basiron, 45, said the idea came naturally as August marks the start of National Day celebrations. The sisters' coordinated outfits drew attention from fellow voters at the polling centre.

items.title: Malaysia's economy set to stay strong in 2H 2026, says Akmal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economic performance is expected to remain strong in the second half of 2026 (2H 2026), supported by government measures to maintain stable oil supplies, says Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. He said the country recorded 5.6 per cent growth in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), while Bank Negara Malaysia's projection for the year remains between 4.0 and 5.0 per cent. "We have achieved 5.6 per cent economic growth in 1H 2026.

items.title: Sisters steal the spotlight in Rantau, casting votes in Jalur Gemilang style ahead of Merdeka
items.summary: REMBAU, Aug 1 — In a vibrant display of national pride, two siblings turned heads at the polling centre in Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Chung Hua, Rantau today when they showed up dressed head-to-toe in Jalur Gemilang-themed attire, adding a festive splash to the occasion. Born and raised in Rantau, the duo decided to infuse their civic duty with the patriotic spirit of the upcoming National Day celebrations. Eldest sister Zamzarina Basiron, 45, explained that the idea came naturally.

items.title: Negri polls: Voter turnout reaches 37.29pct as at 12pm
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Voter turnout for the Negri Sembilan election reached 37.29 per cent as at 12 pm. The Election Commission, in its hourly update, said 320,627 of the 859,760 eligible ordinary voters had cast their ballots. Early voting on July 28 recorded a turnout of 91.06 per cent, with 14,995 voters casting their ballots.

items.title: Johor Bahru police seek e‑hailing driver to identify passenger accused of insulting Islam
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 1 — Police are tracking down an e-hailing driver to assist in the investigation and identify a suspect linked to a viral video containing remarks allegedly insulting Islam in Johor Bahru. Johor Bahru Selatan police chief ACP Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said the district police headquarters received a report from a police officer at 3.25pm on July 31 after the officer came across the video on social media at about 2.30pm the same day. Anyone with information related to the incident is urged to contact the Johor Bahru Selatan Police Headquarters hotline at 07-2182323 or report the matter at the nearest police station.

items.title: Undang Luak Jelebu dismissed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negri Sembilan (DKU) has accepted the dismissal of Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad as the 16th Undang Luak Jelebu over "adat offences". It also said Maarof had forfeited the Darjah Tertinggi Negeri Sembilan (DTNS), the state's highest honour, which he held by virtue of his office as the Undang Luak Jelebu. The dismissal of the Undang Luak Jelebu follows the recent dismissal of the former Undang Luak Sungai Ujong and the replacement of the former Undang Luak Rembau.

items.title: Petronas fuel supply stable until September, says Azalina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Fuel supplies, including petrol and diesel, at Petronas stations nationwide are expected to remain stable and sufficient until September, says Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Legal and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. Azalina said the Crisis Management Task Force (CMT) under NEAC continued to monitor fuel and energy supply amid the global energy crisis arising from the West Asia conflict. On Malaysia's crude oil and natural gas reserves, she said Petronas estimated the country's crude oil reserves at 3.89 billion barrels of oil equivalent, while total natural gas reserves stood at 13.19 billion barrels of oil equivalent as of Jan 1, 2026.

items.title: Anwar invites Mahatma Gandhi's grandson to visit Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has invited Rajmohan Gandhi, the grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, to visit Malaysia in the first quarter of next year to deliver a lecture on democracy, peace, harmony and values-based leadership. In a social media post today, Anwar said he extended the invitation during a telephone conversation with the 91-year-old Rajmohan, an eminent historian and author. Anwar said the lecture would provide an opportunity for academics, university students and community leaders to benefit from Rajmohan's perspectives on democracy, peaceful coexistence and principled leadership.

items.title: Loke: Voters, not surveys, will decide Negri polls [WATCH]
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The outcome of the Negri Sembilan election would ultimately be determined by voters, not pre-election opinion polls, says DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke. Asked about an Ilham Centre survey that showed unfavourable findings for Pakatan Harapan, he said the people's decision remained the most important factor. We hope for the best possible outcome for PH tonight," he told reporters after casting his ballot for the Mambau seat at SJK(C) Kelpin, Taman Ujong, today.

items.title: Eight illegal migrants caught after crossing from Thailand
items.summary: PASIR PUTEH: Eight undocumented Indonesian migrants who entered Malaysia from Thailand were detained in an operation at a house in Kampung Gong Serapat here yesterday. General Operations Force Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the 10 suspects were arrested during the operation codenamed Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan. Ahmad Radzi said police also seized 10 mobile phones worth RM22,000 during the operation.

items.title: Civil servants begin hybrid work arrangement today [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Hybrid Workday (HBH) Policy for civil servants takes effect today, allowing employees to work three days in the office and two days from home or alternative locations. The Public Service Department (PSD) described the policy as a future-ready measure to ensure government services remain resilient amid global changes and evolving work practices, while maintaining service quality. For Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu, Sundays and Thursdays will be compulsory office attendance days.

items.title: Bersatu can win several seats today, says Tun Faisal
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A Bersatu leader has voiced confidence that the party can win several seats in today's Negri Sembilan election. Its information chief, Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz, said this confidence stemmed from positive voter response towards the party's candidates. The Sikamat seat sees a three-cornered fight between Tun Faisal, Pakatan Harapan's Nor Azman Mohamad and Perikatan Nasional's Datuk Razali Abu Samah.

items.title: Civil servants swap desks for hybrid rhythm as SPOT‑Me tracks Malaysia’s new workday experiment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — The Hybrid Workday (HBH) Policy comes into force today, allowing civil servants to work three days in the office and two days from home or alternative locations. The Public Service Department (JPA) described the implementation of the HBH Policy as a future-proof measure to ensure government service delivery remains resilient amid global changes and the evolution of modern working methods, without compromising the quality of services provided to the people. Under the HBH Implementation Guidelines, states observing Sunday as the weekly holiday will have Monday and Friday designated as compulsory office attendance days.

items.title: Masidi: 40pct revenue issue likely to come up at Monday's Sabah-Putrajaya meet
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah will meet with the federal government on Monday to discuss matters related to the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), says Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun. Earlier, Masidi represented Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor at the launch of the state-level National Day and Sabah Day celebrations. In April, the Court of Appeal allowed the federal government's application to stay a High Court order requiring a review of Sabah's 40 per cent revenue entitlement.

items.title: Licensed hunter urges cooperation as Sibu crocodile chase draws roadside crowds, sparks traffic chaos
items.summary: SIBU, Aug 1 — Licensed crocodile hunter Jeferry Siew has appealed for public cooperation after roadside crowds gathered along Jalan Oya–Sibu Jaya during a crocodile capture operation on Thursday evening, causing traffic congestion and raising safety concerns. Siew said many motorists stopped and parked along the roadside to watch the operation, disrupting traffic flow along the busy stretch of road. Jeferry Siew and his team in action, trying to capture the elusive crocodile.

items.title: 'Last year I lost my son, now his wife and child are gone too'
items.summary: Maria Yusoff, 42, and her 11-year-old son Muhammad Ziekry Iman Abli were among three people killed when the Perodua Myvi they were travelling in collided with a diesel tanker at Km25 of the Gua Musang-Kuala Krai road at 7am. Maria's mother-in-law, Rokiah Jusoh, 76, said the tragedy came less than a year after her son, Abli Abdullah, died suddenly from a heart attack on July 27 last year. Rokiah said the family initially withheld news of Maria's death, fearing the shock could affect her health.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan polls see 28.11pc turnout by 11am, says EC
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Voter turnout in the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election stood at 28.11 per cent as of 11am today, according to Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun. He said observations at several polling centres around Seremban showed encouraging participation in the morning, with senior citizens making up a larger number of voters compared to younger voters. “We want to assess the system across different groups of voters, including senior citizens and younger voters.

items.title: Govt success measured by people's gains, says Hajiji
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The true measure of a government's success lies in how much its people benefit from development, says Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. He said the state government would continue strengthening initiatives that directly impact lives, including in education, welfare, housing, healthcare, rural development, women and youth empowerment, and basic amenities. "Ultimately, the true measure of a government's success is not what it has built, but the extent to which the people benefit from that development," he said in a speech delivered by Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun.

items.title: EC chairman monitors Negri polls as voting gets underway
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun today visited three polling centres in Seremban to monitor the voting process and ensure the 16th Negri Sembilan election runs smoothly and orderly. Ramlan then visited Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama Sheikh Haji Mohd Said, also in Sikamat, before concluding his tour at Sekolah Menengah Agama (SMA) Dato' Klana Petra Maamor, which serves the Ampangan constituency. During the visits, he received briefings from election officials on the voting process and inspected facilities provided for voters and election personnel.

items.title: Teacher clings to life in Pasir Mas well as firefighters stage dramatic morning rescue
items.summary: The woman, a teacher at a secondary school near Pasir Mas, lost her footing and plunged into the 5.48-meter-deep well, located behind her kitchen at approximately 7.50am. The Pasir Mas Fire and Rescue Department received the distress call and deployed a team of six firefighters, led by senior fire officer I Asraf Mat Naizi, who arrived at the scene just six minutes later. The woman was carefully hoisted out of the narrow well, and luckily suffered only minor injuries.

items.title: Election Commission chief Ramlan Harun inspects Negeri Sembilan polls
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun today visited three polling centres in Seremban to monitor the voting process and ensure the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election is proceeding smoothly and in an orderly manner. Ramlan then visited Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama Sheikh Haji Mohd Said, also in the Sikamat constituency, before concluding his tour at Sekolah Menengah Agama (SMA) Dato’ Klana Petra Maamor, which serves the Ampangan state constituency. During the visits, he received briefings from election officials on the voting process and inspected the facilities provided for voters and election personnel.

items.title: Police probe dog’s death during stray capture operation in Port Klang
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 1 — Police have opened an investigation paper into the death of a dog during a stray dog capture operation in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Port Klang, three days ago, following allegations of animal cruelty. South Klang police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said the dog was confirmed dead after the incident, which occurred at about 10.50 pm on July 29 in front of a house in the residential area. He said the operation was carried out by the Royal Klang City Council (MBDK) with the cooperation of residents.

items.title: Trump's legal crusade against news media falters
items.summary: NEW YORK: Donald Trump's early legal wins against broadcasters ABC and CBS have given way to defeats and retreats as courts and newsrooms act to protect press freedom. At the end of July, the Justice Department withdrew subpoenas issued to New York Times journalists who had written articles about the security of Trump's presidential aircraft. But most legal experts agree that the courts could have thrown out Trump's claims.

items.title: HKL refutes viral video claims of filthy toilets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — Hospital Kuala Lumpur (HKL) has denied claims that its public toilets are dirty and poorly maintained, as alleged in a video that went viral on Facebook yesterday. In a statement today, HKL director Datuk Dr Harikrishna K. R. Nair said the hospital management had taken note of the allegations and conducted a thorough investigation. “The investigation into all public toilet facilities under HKL’s management found that the toilet shown in the viral video is not located within any facility under HKL’s supervision.

items.title: Siblings lose mother, youngest brother in Gua Musang crash a year after father's death
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Aug 1 — Exactly one year after losing their father, three siblings have been dealt another devastating blow with the deaths of their mother and youngest sibling in a road accident along the Gua Musang-Kuala Krai road near Gua Sejuk here yesterday. Their uncle, Mohamad Faizol Yusoff, 34, said his sister, Maria Yusoff, 42, had been raising her four children, aged between 11 and 21, on her own after her husband died of illness last year. Mohamad Faizol also said he and his siblings would take care of Maria’s children.

items.title: Top leaders cast votes as Negeri Sembilan heads to polls
items.summary: Aminuddin, who is also the Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Linggi state seat, arrived at the polling centre at 8.59am. Also having cast their votes were Foreign Minister and Barisan Nasional (BN) deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, who is contesting the Rantau state seat, and the BN candidate for Linggi, Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli. The Linggi state seat is seeing a three-cornered contest involving Aminuddin, Mohd Faizal, and Datuk Zamri Md Said from Bersatu, while the Rantau seat features a straight fight between Mohamad and PH candidate Dr Azizul Hakim Mahdi.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan caretaker MB Aminuddin casts ballot, says Pakatan confident despite predictions
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Voting began this morning in the 16th Negri Sembilan state election, with caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun saying Pakatan Harapan (PH) remained unfazed by forecasts and external analyses. Aminuddin added that PH was not affected by outside speculation and expressed confidence the coalition could secure more than 19 seats. In Linggi, he faces a three-cornered contest against Barisan Nasional incumbent Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli and Bersatu’s Datuk Zamri Md Said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan state election: Early voter turnout at 8.29pc by 9am
items.summary: The Election Commission (EC), in a Facebook post, said Labu recorded the highest turnout so far at 10.4 per cent, followed by Senaling (10.3 per cent) and Ampangan (9.4 per cent). Rantau recorded the lowest turnout at 6.4 per cent. For comparison, the voter turnout recorded at the same time during the 15th Negeri Sembilan State Election was 9.49 per cent, involving 79,557 out of 838,200 registered voters.

items.title: Female teacher found dead in Hulu Selangor school, police probe incident in staff room
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 1 — A female teacher in her 30s was found dead at a school here yesterday morning after police received an emergency call at about 7.15am. Hulu Selangor district police chief Superintendent M Manimaran said the victim was taken to Hospital Kuala Kubu Bharu but was pronounced dead at the emergency unit, Harian Metro reported. Police urged anyone with information to contact the nearest station, the Hulu Selangor district police headquarters at 03 60641222, or Kerling police station chief Sergeant Major Halim Khan Hazam Khan at 03 60481222.

items.title: Veterinary Services Department denies involvement in government order documents, fake supply
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 1 —The Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) categorically denies the department’s involvement in any physical government order documents or suspicious supply instructions issued outside the official system. “DVS takes seriously complaints regarding attempts at fraud that misuse the names and positions of DVS officers as well as fake government order documents to deceive suppliers into providing supplies and services supposedly for the department’s programmes” according to the statement. DVS also advises suppliers to contact the DVS headquarters, Putrajaya directly at 03-8870 2000 or via email at pro@dvs.gov.my, if there are any doubts regarding the procurement documents received.

items.title: Tabung Haji welcomes RCI recommendations, says already distributes profits based on audited results
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — Lembaga Tabung Haji’s (TH) profit distribution is only announced based on audited financial results, thus strengthening the integrity of the financial reporting process and increasing depositors’ confidence in the institution. The pilgrimage board said the RCI recommended that profit distributions be declared only based on audited financial statements, in line with the principles of good governance, transparency and financial sustainability. TH said that, according to the RCl report, TH’s financial statements for the 2017 financial year did not fully adopt the Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS).

items.title: PM Anwar: No Cabinet objections to programmes for Malays, Islam
items.summary: JEMPOL, Aug 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Cabinet has never objected to any proposal to implement programmes related to Islam or the Malays throughout more than three and a half years of the Madani Government’s administration. Anwar said this during the PH ceramah for the Jeram Padang state constituency in conjunction with the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election near Bahau here last night, which was also attended by PH candidate for the seat, G. Manivannan. Meanwhile, Anwar called on voters to continue supporting PH candidates to ensure close cooperation between the Federal Government and the Negeri Sembilan government could continue.

items.title: Employment agent survives 33rd‑floor fall in Brickfields, semi‑conscious with fractures as police investigate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — A man was seriously injured after reportedly falling from the 33rd floor of a building in Brickfields yesterday. According to Harian Metro , Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said the 32-year-old employment agent is in stable condition and receiving treatment at Hospital Kuala Lumpur. He said police have yet to record a statement from the victim as he remains under medical care.

items.title: Malaysia’s fuel supply stable till September amid energy crisis, says law minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 1 — The supply of fuel (including petrol and diesel) at Petronas gas stations nationwide is expected to be stable and sufficient until September, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Legal and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. She said this network covers about 50 per cent of the country’s domestic fuel needs supplied by Petronas through its publicly listed subsidiary Petronas Dagangan Bhd. As for Low’s question about the amount of crude oil and natural gas reserves in Malaysia and the estimated lifespan of each reserve based on the current production rate, she said that, according to Petronas, Malaysia’s crude oil reserves are estimated at 3.89 billion barrels of oil equivalent, while the estimated total natural gas reserves are as much as 13.19 billion barrels of oil equivalent as of Jan 1, 2026.

items.title: Voting begins in Negeri Sembilan: A decisive day for 859,760 voters
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Voters in Negeri Sembilan will fulfill their democratic rights and civic duty today in the 16th State Election (PRN) to elect their new people’s representatives. A total of 36 State Legislative Assembly (DUN) seats are being contested in this state election, involving 103 candidates. In this state election, 22 state seats face three-cornered fights, another 11 seats feature straight fights, and two seats each witness four-cornered and five-cornered contests.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan polling opens across 401 centres in battle for 36 seats
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — A total of 401 polling centres involving 1,668 streams for the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election opened simultaneously at 8am today, with 859,760 registered voters, including 7,391 postal voters, eligible to cast their ballots in the contest for the 36 state seats. The 16th Negeri Sembilan state election sees 103 candidates, with Pakatan Harapan (PH) contesting all 36 seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (BN) with 25, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) with 24, Perikatan Nasional (PN) with 11, and four independent candidates. For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan votes today: 10 seats to watch in pivotal state election
items.summary: All 36 state seats are at stake, with the outcome carrying significance beyond Negeri Sembilan. Linggi (PH-PKR vs BN-Umno vs Bersatu) Linggi is expected to be one of the election’s defining contests after caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun left his long-held Sikamat seat to contest there. — Picture by Choo Choy May Pertang (BN-Umno vs PH-PKR vs Bersatu) Another closely watched contest is Pertang, where Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias is seeking re-election against PH’s Mohd Umry Abdul Khois and Bersatu’s Mohd Faizal Fadli Mohd Idrus.

items.title: Malaysia records 2,001 factory fires, RM4.21b losses since 2020, says Fire Dept D-G
items.summary: To strengthen compliance with fire safety aspects, he said the JBPM continues to enhance industrial premises inspection activities. He said that a total of 1,878 factory premises were inspected in 2025 compared to 1,563 premises the previous year. “During the same period, the number of premises issued with Fire Hazard Elimination Notices (MBK) increased from 706 premises in 2024 to 1,191 premises in 2025,” he said.

items.title: EC reminds Negeri Sembilan voters to follow recommended times, phones barred during voting
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 31 — The Election Commission (EC) has reminded voters in Negeri Sembilan to vote early or at their recommended voting times, while adhering to rules prohibiting mobile phone use and campaign materials at polling stations during tomorrow’s state election. However, they may vote anytime during polling hours from 8 am to 6 pm, depending on their polling centre’s operating hours. The EC said 15,344 polling officials will be responsible for conducting the voting process at 401 polling centres.
